items.title: Skipper, Airbnb’s embedded workflow engine, is now open source

items.title: Pick Problems That Survive When AI Solves Coding - Ara Khan, Cline
items.content_snippet: What will you work on once frontier labs solve coding? Girish Konda maps each failure to the distributed-systems idea that already explains it, with examples from his open-source MCP Pacemaker and the MCP and A2A specs. items.title: Your Team's Agents Are All Shipping to the Same Code at Once - Patrick Debois, Tessl
items.content_snippet: Your whole team runs coding agents now, and all of them land on the same main branch. Continuous delivery wasn't built for that. Patrick Debois maps what breaks when a software factory goes multiplayer, and the patterns that fix it: one main for the agents, one board for the people. Patrick Debois, Tessl: https://x.com/patrickdebois | https://tessl.io

items.title: Every Company Is Building Agents That Can't Work Together - Justin Schroeder, Standard Agents
items.content_snippet: Skills and MCP gave agents a standard way to get context, but the agents themselves are still one-offs: every team builds its own, and none of them can be shared or combined. Justin Schroeder argues that agents won't reach their potential without portability and composition, and walks through a concrete agent runtime standard that lets anyone build an agent, distribute it, and compose it with others. Justin Schroeder, Standard Agents: https://x.com/jpschroeder | https://standardagents.ai
